sources.citation: Hammarström et al. 2025. Glottolog 5.3, languoid nget1241 (Ngete) + langdoc listing
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: one reference (Caprile & Jungraithmayr 1973, Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist), zero descriptive works; alt names Ka'do Ngueté, Nge'dé, Nguetté, Ngueté, Zime.

sources.citation: Lovestrand, Joseph. 2026. Directional extensions in Chadic languages. Berlin: Language Science Press (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19336900), Appendix C, '2 South Masa'
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; states verbatim: 'No relevant publications were found for Ngete (nget1241) and the publications on Mesme (mesm1239) either do not cover the verbal morphology or were inaccessible.'

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phoneme tables are for the He'dé dialect (from Sachnine 1982), not Ngete; no tone or stress section. Lists varieties Dzəpaw/Lamé, Ngeté (Sorga-Ngeté), He'dé (Heɗe-Rong) citing Blench 2006 AALIST.

sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds). 2016. Ethnologue 19th ed., entry Ngete [nnn] (Internet Archive copy); also 22nd ed. 2019 copy
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. 10,000 (1991 UBS); east of Pala, Ngeté village area; 'Dialects: None known. Linguistic and sociolinguistic differences with Pévé [lme] and Herdé [hed]'; no language-development (grammar/literacy/NT) entries listed.

sources.citation: Shryock, Aaron. 1997. The classification of the Masa group of languages. Studies in African Linguistics 26(1): 29-62
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Does not mention Ngete by name; Masa-group tone lexical on nouns, grammatical on verbs (p.43); nothing on stress. Its bibliography gives Hufnagel 1986 ms 'Comparative reconstruction of Zime, Kado, and Peve'.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 1987. [paper on Zime/Ngete verbal aspect] In H. Jungraithmayr & W. W. Müller (eds), Proceedings of the Fourth International Hamito-Semitic Congress (Marburg, 20-22 September 1983). Amsterdam: John Benjamins (CILT 44).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher (DOI); library e-access not checked
sources.note: Contains Ngete aspect paradigms with tone (H/M contrast partly replaced by a/i vowel opposition in Ngete); preview/snippet only on Google Books; paywalled at Benjamins.

sources.citation: Hufnagel, Ruth. 1986. Comparative reconstruction of Zime, Kado, and Peve. Unpublished ms., Mission Protestante, Kélo, Chad.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Cited by Shryock 1995/1997 as the source of Zime-cluster comparative data (likely including Ngete); unpublished mission manuscript, possibly held by SIL Chad.

sources.citation: Hamilton, Mark Reed. 1982. Verbal marking systems in Chadic. (M.A./Ph.D. thesis; publisher not identified.)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Re-uses Jungraithmayr's Ngete/Sorga data with tone marking; secondary, but the only other work found that treats Ngete forms. Google Books eZ5RAAAAMAAJ snippet only.

sources.citation: Sachnine, Michka. 1982. Le lamé (vùn-dzə̀pàò), un parler zimé du Nord-Cameroun (langue tchadique). 1: Phonologie, grammaire; 2: Dictionnaire. Paris: SELAF/ACCT (Langues et cultures africaines 1).

sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The full phonology of the cluster's Cameroonian variety (Lamé/Dzəpaw), the source the earlier scan named; would give the nearest stress/tone statement for the cluster but describes a different variety (herd1236 per Glottolog, peve1243 per WALS). HathiTrust uc1.b4232080/81 search-only.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 1978. The Zime dialect cluster ('Kado', 'Dari') in southern Chad: its verbal aspect system. Afrika und Übersee 61(1): 1-27.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number Philol 14)
sources.note: The only published description containing first-hand Ngete (Sorga-Ngete) data: comparative verbal-aspect system of the Zime dialects with H/M/L tone marking; the introduction may contain a phonological note on tone vs. stress. Google Books snippet-only; A&Ü vol. 61 not scanned on archive.org/HathiTrust full view.

sources.citation: Caprile, Jean-Pierre & Herrmann Jungraithmayr. 1973. Inventaire provisoire des langues 'tchadiques' parlées sur le territoire de la République du Tchad. Africana Marburgensia 6(2): 31-48.
